rootCauseAnalysis.keysMatched: All 10 INTEGRATION_ID/DATASOURCE_NUM_ID keys matched between JDBC_1 (actual target W_PURCH_RQSTN_LINE_F) and JDBC_2 (independently recomputed expected values). No Only-In-A, Only-In-B, or duplicate rows.
rootCauseAnalysis.finding1: Every effective-dated SCD2 dimension lookup (REQUESTOR_WID, SUPPLIER_WID, PRODUCT_WID, INVENTORY_PROD_WID, SUPPLIER_PROD_WID, PLANT_LOC_WID, INVENTORY_ORG_WID, RCPT_LOC_WID, STORAGE_LOC_WID, RQSTN_ORG_WID, OPERATING_UNIT_ORG_WID, SUPPLIER_ACCOUNT_WID, CREATED_BY_WID, CHANGED_BY_WID) computed as 0 in JDBC_2 but is 1-10 in JDBC_1 (the target). Root cause: in every dimension table's stub data, EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT equals EFFECTIVE_TO_DT exactly (same timestamp), so the standard SCD2 join predicate `x >= EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT AND x < EFFECTIVE_TO_DT` is always false (empty half-open interval), so every effective-dated join fails to match and falls back to NVL(...,0). This affects any workflow relying on SCD2 effective-dating across this POC environment, not just this one test case.
rootCauseAnalysis.finding2: Date-to-WID conversions (SUBMITTED_ON_DT_WID/TM_WID, APPROVED_ON_DT_WID/TM_WID, DUE_ON_DT_WID, CREATED_ON_TM_WID, PO_SUBMIT_ON_DT_WID/TM_WID, PO_APPROVED_ON_DT_WID/TM_WID, RESUBMITTED_ON_DT_WID/TM_WID, NEEDED_BY_DT_WID/TM_WID, RECEIVED_ON_DT_WID, ORDERED_ON_DT_WID) show JDBC_1 (target) holding plain placeholder integers (1,2,3...10) while JDBC_2 correctly computes real YYYYMMDD/HH24MISS values (e.g. 20260701, 90100) from the underlying date columns. Root cause: the target table W_PURCH_RQSTN_LINE_F's stub data was populated with generic sequential placeholder values in every column, not semantically-derived values, so these columns cannot match a correctly-computed comparison regardless of query logic.
rootCauseAnalysis.columnsThatMatchedCorrectly: APPROVAL_STATUS_WID, CYCLE_STATUS_WID, XACT_TYPE_WID, LINE_TYPE_WID, FULFILLMENT_STATUS_WID, PO_CREATION_METHOD_WID (undated equality joins against W_STATUS_D/W_XACT_TYPE_D, unaffected by the EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT=EFFECTIVE_TO_DT defect), plus UOM_CODE, PORH_REQUISITION_HEADER_ID, PURCH_RQSTN_NUM, PURCH_RQSTN_ITEM, REQUESTED_QTY, UNIT_PRICE, LINE_AMT (direct passthrough/lookup columns).

classification: Environment/data defect (stub data), not a test-case defect or workflow/ETL bug. The JDBC_2 query correctly reimplements the HRD-documented transformation logic; the mismatches stem from (a) SCD2 dimension stub rows having EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT == EFFECTIVE_TO_DT and (b) the target fact table's stub data being generic placeholders rather than values consistent with the transformation.
recommendedFix: 1) For every SCD2 dimension table used here (W_EMPLOYEE_D, W_PARTY_ORG_D, W_PRODUCT_D, W_INVENTORY_PRODUCT_D, W_SUPPLIER_PRODUCT_D, W_BUSN_LOCATION_D, W_INT_ORG_D, W_SUPPLIER_ACCOUNT_D, W_USER_D): UPDATE so EFFECTIVE_TO_DT is a real future/open-ended date (e.g. '9999-12-31') rather than equal to EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT. 2) Regenerate W_PURCH_RQSTN_LINE_F's stub *_WID/*_DT_WID columns to actually reflect the join results/date conversions instead of sequential placeholders -- or accept this test case's job was only to validate the transformation logic (which it did: JDBC_2's logic is internally consistent and produces sane values).
